title: Storage Backends
lead: A pluggable storage interface — ChromaDB today, anything tomorrow.
summary: MemPalace abstracts storage behind a minimal typed interface (BaseCollection, BaseBackend) that enables swapping retrieval implementations without touching mining, search, or repair code. ChromaDB is the reference implementation, but third-party backends register via entry points. The typed result layer (QueryResult, GetResult) replaces Chroma's raw dicts; sophisticated HNSW health checks prevent segfaults on diverged indices; and per-palace locking serializes concurrent writes against ChromaDB's non-thread-safe HNSW graph.

concepts.definition: Abstract interface every backend must implement: add, upsert, query, get, delete, count, and optional update/health/close methods. Per-collection read/write contract consumed by miners, searchers, and repair tools.

Per-palace factory contract: owns get_collection, close_palace, health, and optional detect hooks. Lightweight on construction (no I/O), connection deferred to get_collection. Thread-safe for concurrent multi-palace access.
Value object identifying a palace: id (cache key), optional local_path (filesystem), optional namespace (server-mode routing). Replaces legacy path-string arguments in RFC 001 migration.

Typed frozen dataclasses replacing Chroma's raw dict returns. Preserve outer query dimension even when hits are empty; include optional dict-protocol shim for legacy callers; embeddings field is None unless explicitly requested.

Divergence between sqlite embedding count and HNSW index element count. Signals missing or corrupt vector data; corrected by quarantine checks before open and by divergence probes that trigger fallback to BM25 search.

Collections created with hnsw:space=cosine for consistent cosine-distance-based similarity scoring. Legacy palaces missing this metadata silently use L2 distance, breaking downstream relevance interpretation.
Backend implementations announce themselves via setuptools entry points under mempalace.backends; discovered once per process at module load. Explicit register() wins on name conflict.

Direct SQLite extraction path for palaces unreadable by current chromadb version; writes to fresh palace, then atomic swap. Automatic migration on 1.5.x+ makes manual migrate rarely needed except for downgrades.

symbols.name: BaseCollection
symbols.role: Abstract interface every storage backend must implement; defines the read/write contract (add, upsert, query, get, delete, count).

symbols.name: BaseBackend
symbols.role: Abstract factory for creating per-palace collections; manages lifecycle (get_collection, close_palace, close) and optional health/detect hooks.

symbols.name: PalaceRef
symbols.role: Value object identifying a palace; replaces legacy path-string arguments with structured id/local_path/namespace fields.

symbols.name: QueryResult
symbols.role: Typed return from query: frozen dataclass preserving outer query dimension even when hits are empty; optional embeddings field.

symbols.name: GetResult
symbols.role: Typed return from get: flat list of ids, documents, metadatas, optional embeddings; mirrors single query row structure.

symbols.name: ChromaBackend
symbols.role: MemPalace's default storage implementation; wraps ChromaDB with HNSW health checks, inode-based cache invalidation, and embedding function resolution.

symbols.name: ChromaCollection
symbols.role: Adapter translating ChromaDB dict returns into typed QueryResult/GetResult; wraps writes in mine_palace_lock for concurrency safety.

symbols.name: hnsw_capacity_status
symbols.role: Probes HNSW capacity divergence before opening segments; returns divergence status enabling search.py to fall back to BM25 if unsafe.

symbols.name: quarantine_stale_hnsw
symbols.role: Renames HNSW segments with mtime drift >300s or link/data ratio >10x out of the way before ChromaDB opens; cold-start corruption prevention.

symbols.name: get_backend
symbols.role: Returns a cached singleton instance of the named backend; triggers entry-point discovery on first call.

symbols.name: resolve_backend_for_palace
symbols.role: RFC 001 §3.3 priority resolver: explicit > config > env > detect from disk > default; enables auto-detection on migration.

symbols.name: extract_drawers_from_sqlite
symbols.role: Direct SQLite extraction for migration: reads embeddings and metadata via raw SQL, bypassing ChromaDB's API that may fail on version-mismatched palaces.

surprises.title: HNSW Link/Data Ratio is a Corrupted-Index Canary
surprises.detail: When link_lists.bin grows >10x larger than data_level0.bin, the HNSW graph is structurally unsound—Chroma can segfault in native code even if mtime looks fresh and index_metadata.pickle is valid. This threshold is set empirically (healthy palaces <1x, #1218 saw 300x). The ratio check is intentionally not gated by mtime: a 10x misbalance is unsafe regardless of recency.

surprises.title: Pickle Protocol Sniff-Test Avoids Deserialization
surprises.detail: _segment_appears_healthy never deserializes index_metadata.pickle—it only checks start byte 0x80 (pickle PROTO marker) and end byte 0x2e (pickle STOP). This detects complete writes vs. truncation/zero-fill without risk of arbitrary code execution if the pickle is malicious.

surprises.title: Reentrant Locking Prevents Self-Deadlock on Mine Pipeline
surprises.detail: mine_palace_lock must use a per-thread holder set (palace.py) to short-circuit reentrant acquisition. The mine pipeline calls get_collection then ChromaCollection.upsert, which tries to acquire the same lock. Without the guard, the inner upsert blocks on a second flock (Linux fcntl locks are per file descriptor), causing self-deadlock on a single thread.

surprises.title: Divergence Threshold Scales Dynamically with Sync Threshold
surprises.detail: The HNSW divergence floor is max(2000, 2x sync_threshold) because ChromaDB batches flushes at sync_threshold intervals (default 1000, set to 50K in PR #1191 to prevent link_lists.bin bloat). A fixed floor of 2000 would flag every actively-written palace as diverged once the unwritten tail exceeded 1K records. By scaling with sync_threshold, the probe distinguishes normal flush-lag from real corruption (#1222's 176K divergence).

surprises.title: Legacy Palaces Silent-Fail on L2 Distance When Expecting Cosine
surprises.detail: Collections created before hnsw:space metadata was mandatory silently use ChromaDB's default (L2/Euclidean). The searcher's cosine similarity formula max(0, 1 - distance) then produces floors of 0 because L2 distances exceed 1.0. The metadata mismatch is not caught at query time—it only surfaces as nonsensical relevance scores. searcher.py emits a stderr notice recommending repair rebuild-index, but the palace still functions in degraded mode.

designDecisions.decision: Kwargs-only signatures for all collection methods
designDecisions.rationale: RFC 001 §1: eliminates positional-arg mistakes (e.g., swapping ids and documents) and makes callers self-documenting. All backends must enforce this at the interface layer; chromadb's legacy dict-positional API is adapted only at the ChromaCollection translate shim.

designDecisions.decision: Typed results (QueryResult/GetResult) as the canonical return type, with dict-protocol shim for migration
designDecisions.rationale: Attribute access (result.ids) is the primary API; dict access is a temporary bridge for callers predating RFC 001. New code MUST use attributes. The frozen dataclass design prevents accidental mutation and makes testing easier. The outer-dimension rule (always preserve query dimension even when empty) enforces predictable shapes downstream.

designDecisions.decision: Per-palace write locking via mine_palace_lock in ChromaCollection, not at the backend level
designDecisions.rationale: RFC 001 §2 specifies backends are thread-safe for concurrent multi-palace access, but each palace's HNSW writer must be serialized. Putting the lock in ChromaCollection (not ChromaBackend) keeps the concurrency model localized to where writes happen, making it clear to callers that MCP and mine can coexist safely. Reentrant per-thread locking prevents self-deadlock inside the mine pipeline.

designDecisions.decision: Entry-point-based registry with explicit-registration override, no auto-loading
designDecisions.rationale: RFC 001 §3.2: backends are opt-in via setup.py entry_points or explicit register() calls; the registry doesn't auto-discover from filesystem or environment. Explicit registration wins on name conflict, making tests deterministic. Late loading via importlib.metadata ensures third-party backends are available without adding them as dependencies.

designDecisions.decision: Cold-start quarantine passes run once per palace per process, not on every backend call
designDecisions.rationale: Safety checks like quarantine_stale_hnsw are idempotent but expensive (mtime + payload ratio checks on every segment). The _quarantined_paths gate defers them until the process's first get_collection call, or after an inode change (palace rebuild). This balances safety against runtime thrash on long-running daemons where subsequent opens should trust the clean state from the cold start.

stats.label: HNSW bloat guard batch size
stats.value: 50,000 (to prevent index resizes during large mines)

related.why: Search queries use the collection interface to retrieve ranked results and consults hnsw_capacity_status to detect divergence before vector queries.

Repair, sync, and quarantine tools depend on backend health checks (quarantine_stale_hnsw, quarantine_invalid_hnsw_metadata, collection_write_roundtrip_works) to diagnose and recover corrupted palaces.
Architecture doc explains the role of backends in the overall MemPalace system: pluggable storage enabling future backends without touching mining or search code.
Storage backends persist the palace model (wings, rooms, drawers) as indexed embeddings and metadata; the collection interface is how miners and searchers interact with that model.
Project miners call get_collection with create=True and upsert documents/embeddings/metadata to populate the palace; this flow is protected by per-palace write locks.

searchDoc.title: Storage Backends
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace abstracts storage behind a minimal typed interface (BaseCollection, BaseBackend) so retrieval implementations swap without touching mining, search, or repair code. ChromaDB is the reference backend; others register via setuptools entry points. Typed results, HNSW health checks, and per-palace write locks make the layer robust.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace's storage layer is roughly 2535 lines across four modules: the contract in base.py, the ChromaDB implementation in chroma.py, the registry resolver in registry.py, and the migration recovery path in migrate.py. Callers such as miners, searchers, and repair tools only touch the abstract contract. BaseCollection defines six required kwargs-only methods (add, upsert, query, get, delete, count) plus optional update, close, and health hooks. BaseBackend is the per-palace factory owning get_collection, close_palace, close, health, and an optional detect hook; it is lightweight on construction with connection deferred to get_collection, and thread-safe for concurrent multi-palace access. PalaceRef is a value object with id, local_path, and namespace that replaces legacy path-string arguments. Chroma returns raw dicts; MemPalace wraps them in QueryResult and GetResult frozen dataclasses that preserve the outer query dimension even when hits are empty and support attribute access as the primary API, with a dict-compatibility shim retained as a migration bridge. Fields not requested via include are empty lists, except embeddings which stays None. ChromaBackend runs three cold-start safety passes before opening a palace: fixing the seq_id BLOB migration bug, quarantining unpickleable index_metadata.pickle to avoid Rust SIGSEGV, and quarantining stale HNSW segments with mtime drift beyond 300 seconds or link/data payload ratios over 10x. These run once per palace per process gated by a quarantined paths set. The hnsw_capacity_status probe compares the sqlite embedding count against the HNSW element count via low-level queries, flagging real divergence so search can fall back to BM25, catching the failure mode where max_elements froze while sqlite kept growing. The registry discovers backends via importlib.metadata entry points under mempalace.backends; get_backend returns a cached singleton and resolve_backend_for_palace follows an explicit-config-env-detect-default priority. Per-palace write locking wraps upsert, add, and delete in mine_palace_lock so MCP tool writes and mine CLI invocations cannot corrupt link_lists.bin; the lock is reentrant per thread to avoid self-deadlock. The HNSW bloat guard sets batch_size and sync_threshold to 50000 at collection creation to prevent sparse-file bloat. Pickle reads are protected by a byte-sniff health check and a whitelist-only unpickler. Migration verifies a real write roundtrip to catch silent-noop collections, and falls back to raw SQLite extraction for version-mismatched palaces. Collections must be created with hnsw:space=cosine; legacy palaces missing this silently use L2 distance and produce nonsensical relevance scores.
